title: The Skyline Problem
summary: Given the locations and heights of all buildings, return the skyline formed by these buildings when viewed from a distance.
statement: Given the locations and heights of all buildings, return the skyline formed by these buildings when viewed from a distance. The skyline is represented as a list of "key points" sorted by their x-coordinate, where each key point is the left endpoint of some horizontal segment in the skyline. The last point in the list has a y-coordinate of 0, marking the termination of the skyline. Ensure that there are no consecutive horizontal lines of equal height in the output skyline.
constraints: 1–10000 buildings [left,right,height], sorted by nondecreasing left. 0 ≤ left < right ≤ 2^31-1 and 1 ≤ height ≤ 2^31-1. Buildings may coincide or overlap.
Return increasing-x key points [x,current_max_height], including zero-height gaps and the final drop to zero. Combine all events at the same x and omit consecutive points with the same height.
hints: The skyline changes only at building endpoints, and the visible height is the maximum currently active height.
Sweep endpoints in increasing x while a max-heap tracks active buildings and their right edges.
At each x insert all started buildings, remove expired heap tops, and emit the resulting height only if it differs from the previous height.
Process every start/end at the same coordinate before emitting a point; adjacent equal-height segments must merge.
editorial: A heap ordered by negative height exposes the tallest active building. Expired shorter buildings may remain buried until they reach the top; removing expired tops is sufficient for the current maximum. All starts and ends at the same x are resolved together, and unchanged heights are omitted. Each building enters and leaves at most once, while endpoint sorting costs O(n log n). The independent oracle scans all buildings at every distinct endpoint, directly measuring the geometric upper envelope instead of maintaining an active heap.

tests.explanation: The highest active building changes at 2,3,7,12,15,20,24. The point [12,0] records the ground gap before the next building at 15.
Touching buildings of equal height form one segment: [0,3] then [5,0], with no redundant point at x=2.
